item.title: The FIMA trigger has a number now, and the trade just broke Bitcoin's way
item.dc:creator: Kairos
item.description: Arthur Hayes says the $60 billion FIMA repo cap is the next Bitcoin liquidity trigger, while Macro's hammering of the rate-hike trade removed the single biggest headwind this asset has been fighting.
item.content:encoded:
Arthur Hayes says the $60 billion FIMA repo cap is the next Bitcoin liquidity trigger, while Macro's hammering of the rate-hike trade removed the single biggest headwind this asset has been fighting.

Yesterday four models were converging on two different floors and nobody was sure which one would bind first. Today the arguments about direction got quieter because the picture around them shifted.

Market context. Per the Crypto PM list, Bitcoin spot held roughly $64,000 with Market Outlook number 89 carrying a read of $65,310 against ETH at $1,926, the Nasdaq 100 at $29,838, gold at $4,355 and dollar-yen at 158.49. The key levels are two-sided. Support sits at $62,500 and the February low at $60,000, while the anchored VWAP is at $67,600 and the final boss remains $80,000. Bollinger band width is the narrowest it has been since October 2023.

Per Lookonchain, US Bitcoin ETFs shed 1,132 coins on the day, about $72 million, for a seven-day net of minus 202 coins. Ethereum ETFs added 3,947 ETH, about $7.5 million, for a seven-day net of plus 65,941 ETH and about $125 million. The flows have diverged for five straight sessions at the narrowest band in nearly three years, and that is a setup, not an accident.

1. Arthur Hayes just named the FIMA cap as Bitcoin's next trigger, and he gave it a number. Per Scott Melker and the Crypto PM list, Hayes says the $60 billion Fed FIMA repo facility cap is what unlocks the next Bitcoin leg and that a rate hike is not needed for the move, merely an expansion of the facility that lets foreign central banks borrow dollars against Treasuries rather than selling them. The mechanism is the same one Bessent proposed in July for the BOJ's intervention: Japan, the largest foreign holder of Treasuries at about $1.2 trillion, gets to borrow against them instead of selling, which removes the forced seller from the long end and adds dollar liquidity through the back door.

The call lands directly on the Macro edition today. The September hike odds collapsed from 42.1 to 29 percent, the December hike moved from 73.8 to 62.3, and the market is no longer pricing any hike in 2026 above 50 percent. The single biggest headwind Bitcoin has been fighting was a four-hike year. That trade just broke.

Per Cav, open interest relative to market cap is elevated across both perpetuals and Deribit options, and a break above the range will not be a slow stair-step rally. A short cascade is priced into the open interest structure, not just the tweet sentiment.

2. Figure reported and the lending business is growing faster than the price. Per the Crypto PM list, Figure did diluted earnings of 35 cents a share against roughly 25 cents expected. Capital Lending Markets volume hit $4.26 billion, up 132 percent year over year. The net take rate compressed to 3.6 percent from 4.0, adjusted EBITDA came in at $119.4 million at a 54.6 percent margin against 47.2 percent, net income rose to $87 million, up 192 percent, and the lender count reached 489. The company guided third-quarter volume to $4.8 to $5.2 billion and the Kiavi acquisition is pending at $717 million.

Per the house calls ledger, Figure was a catalyst call due today after a run of quarters. The beat clears the bar and the guide says the next quarter is bigger, which makes it a hit on the numbers and leaves the open question of whether the volume growth is priced into a stock that is up substantially on the year.

3. Standard Chartered put a $200 price target on Chainlink, and the reaction was a lot quieter than the number. Per Arbitrage Andy, Standard Chartered initiated coverage on $LINK with a $200 target for 2030, about a 2,400 percent return from the current price near $8, and the argument is that Chainlink becomes the critical data infrastructure for the entire tokenized real-world-asset economy. The report landed the same week that Link quietly crossed a series of integration milestones that the desk has been tracking.

The price is the problem more than the thesis. A coin at $8 with a $200 target is a 24-bagger and that is the kind of number that invites a fade even when the bank putting it up is a real one. VirtualBacon noted today that XRP still has ten times potential, that altcoins outside the top five carry the same return characteristics as 2021 and 2023, and that total altcoin market cap growth follows the Bitcoin market cap expansion whatever the multiple. A coin with a named institutional target at a five-handle price is the shape of the thing his framework is describing.

4. Robinhood Chain is pumping memecoins while the crypto segment that funds it is shrinking. Per 0xResearch and Degen Sensei, Robinhood Chain flipped Base in DEX volume in July, memecoins are 51 percent of spot volume against 5 percent for the real-world assets it was built for, and PumpFun revenue is surging as the chain's fee engine. The other side is the Robinhood corporate numbers. Monthly metrics released after the close showed crypto volumes down substantially, which was expected after a July that was tough across every trading metric, and the crypto segment revenue fell 38 percent year over year to $100 million in Q2.

Per Degen Sensei, Solana reclaimed DEX volume leadership from BNB Chain, on-chain has been strong, and the majors have been printing some of the lowest volatility days in history, which normally means a big move is coming. The sentiment bias is toward a dip before the rip, and the cash the desk has been telling you to keep ready is the same cash he is telling his readers to keep ready.

A fourth voice, Milk Road, noted Solana usage is exploding while price lags. That is the same tension driving the "adoption versus price" deep-dive the Sunday memo carried two weeks ago. The signal has not changed direction.

Single names worth your watchlist.

  • $BTC. At roughly $64,000 with support at $62,500 and $60,000, resistance at $67,600 and $80,000, in its narrowest Bollinger band since October 2023. ETF outflows of 1,132 coins on the day against the September hike trade collapsing in Macro.
  • $FIGR. 35 cents of diluted earnings against 25 expected, $4.26 billion of lending volume up 132 percent, and a guide of $4.8 to $5.2 billion for Q3. The Kiavi close at $717 million and the ARC mainnet on September 16 with BlackRock, Visa and DTCC as validators.
  • $LINK. Standard Chartered $200 target for 2030 on a thesis of critical data infrastructure for tokenized RWAs. At $8, the target is 24 times the price and a real bank is standing behind it.
  • $STRC. Brazil's largest Bitcoin treasury firm is planning an ETF with 95 percent allocation to Strategy, and the house has been tracking the treasury-company unwind-to-accumulation shift since last week.
  • $HOOD. Its chain leads L2 fee revenue and PumpFun is the engine while the corporate crypto segment shrank 38 percent to $100 million. The memo on this is that the chain is a memecoin chain wearing an RWA costume, and the corporate numbers confirm it.

item.title: A fourth model puts the low at $56,000, below the leg I have been carrying
item.dc:creator: Kairos
item.description: Jesse Eckel dates the capitulation to October on a 200-day convergence and rules out $40,000 outright, because this drawdown is already far shallower than 2017 or 2021.
item.content:encoded:
Jesse Eckel dates the capitulation to October on a 200-day convergence and rules out $40,000 outright, because this drawdown is already far shallower than 2017 or 2021.

Yesterday three independent frameworks converged on $67,000 as the flip. Today a fourth arrived, ignored that level entirely, and put the bottom below the one I have been carrying.

Market context. Per the Financial Markets morning list, three separate on-chain transfers imply Bitcoin at $63,611, $63,693 and $63,814, so call it $63,700 and unchanged. Bollinger band width is the narrowest since October 2023.

The leverage map is the tradeable part. Per the Crypto morning list, four bears are short a combined 5,375 coins, about $343 million, with liquidations stacked at $64,101, $64,577, $66,007 and $66,030. Two longs hold 1,547 coins with liquidations down at $61,200 and $61,832. The nearest bear stop sits under one percent above spot and the nearest long stop is four percent below, so the squeeze risk is asymmetrically upward from here.

Flows went the other way. Per the same list, US spot ETFs took $865.3 million over five sessions for a 2.2 percent gain, behind the Nasdaq's 3.0, and have now flipped to $144.6 million of net redemptions.

1. Eckel's low is $56,000 and he dates it to October. Per Jesse Eckel, the test is a convergence rather than a level: price and the 200-day moving average meet around October 2026, exactly one year after this cycle's high. Bitcoin has been below that average since October 2025 and was rejected directly on the line the one time it tried to reclaim it.

His path is a drop from 63 to 64,000 down to about 56,000 in an October capitulation, then a turn. The derivation is decay in the post-chop drawdown across cycles: 51 percent in 2017, 20 percent in 2021, about 12 percent now.

Eckel's cycle arithmeticReading
Days into the bear when the chop began199 in 2017, 219 in 2021, 240 now
Cycle gain579x, then 129x, then 22x, now 8.16x
Chop zone depth below the high67 percent in 2017, 72 in 2021, 49 now

That last row is why he rules out $40,000 and $30,000 for this cycle outright. A drawdown already this shallow does not, on his own decay logic, produce a 2018-style flush.

This is same-direction confirmation of my 60/40 for $58,000 before $75,000, and it is also a warning about my timing. He agrees the low is lower and he puts it in October, not this week. Note also that his flip line is the 200-day, not the $67,000 that On-Chain Mind, VirtualBacon and Sykodelic all landed on yesterday. Four frameworks, two different lines, and nobody has reconciled them. Per the Crypto list, On-Chain Mind himself today switched to a different tool entirely and called Bitcoin "firmly in the Value Zone" at 60 percent of his DCA channel.

I am holding 60/40 and moving nothing. When four models disagree about the line and agree about the direction, the direction is the information.

2. Cramer sold everything on quantum, and the physics says he is early by a decade. Per Milk Road, Jim Cramer said on August 3 that he is selling every last one of his Bitcoin, because quantum computers crack it within about three years. He had interviewed IBM's Arvind Krishna days earlier, who put the window at three to four.

The research genuinely moved. A March paper from Google Quantum AI with the Ethereum Foundation and Stanford put breaking Bitcoin's cryptography at fewer than 500,000 physical qubits and about nine minutes per key, roughly twenty times less hardware than previously estimated. Caltech and a startup called Oratomic claimed 26,000 qubits over ten days on different hardware.

Then the number that settles it for now. The largest key publicly broken on real quantum hardware this year was 15 bits. Bitcoin uses 256. None of the existing machines are error-corrected at anything near that scale.

The exposure is real and old: wallet formats from 2009 and 2010 wrote public keys straight to the chain, and that plus every wallet that has ever sent is about a third of all Bitcoin ever mined, of which roughly 1.1 million coins are Satoshi's and can never be moved. The defence is already merged, with BIP-360 keeping keys off-chain since February 11 and live on testnet with more than fifty miners.

Cramer selling a 256-bit problem on a 15-bit result is a sentiment event, not a security event. The thing that actually moves this asset inside ninety days is the CLARITY cloture vote in mid-September that Macro laid out.

3. Robinhood Chain is a memecoin chain wearing a real-world-asset costume. Two sources published opposite readings of the same chain on the same day, which makes this easy to adjudicate.

Per 0xSammy, the bull case is that Stonkbrokers fees buy Nvidia and Apple shares onchain and distribute them into token-bound wallets, that a new project called Tickeryard went from a $200,000 mint to $4 to $5 million, and that Robinhood Chain dominates EVM chain fees. He discloses he holds many of the assets he names.

Per 0xResearch, Blockworks measured it. Memecoins are 51 percent of Robinhood Chain spot volume against 5 percent for real-world assets, its stated purpose. Known revenue annualises to $54.8 million, about 14 percent of Robinhood's crypto revenue, and Robinhood's Q2 crypto revenue fell 38 percent year over year to $100 million.

One more number closes it. The Stonkbrokers collection this desk logged on Sunday at $80 million fully diluted is quoted today at $54 million, under a piece titled "Explodes."

4. Two businesses onchain are actually earning money, and neither is a memecoin. Per 0xResearch, Circle posted second-quarter revenue and reserve income of $701 million, up 7 percent, adjusted EBITDA of $143 million, USDC supply of $73.3 billion, up 19 percent, and $14.8 trillion of onchain transfer volume, up 151 percent. The stock rose 16 percent on the week to about $71. Two dated catalysts follow: Arc mainnet on September 16 with BlackRock, Visa and DTCC as founding validators, and federal approval of Circle National Trust.

Aptos is the stranger case. It is the only general-purpose chain with positive token-holder net income, at plus $6.33 per $10,000 of fully diluted value against Ethereum at minus $0.95, Solana minus $1.89 and Sui minus $6.18. It got there by repricing gas ten times, halving staking to a flat 2.6 percent and capping supply. Revenue rose about sixteen times while transactions went from 4.5 million a day to over 12 million at ten times the fee. There is no listed proxy, so it is a token trade or nothing. Carry it for the mechanism: a chain raised prices and kept its users.

Single names worth your watchlist.

  • $BTC. At $63,700 in its narrowest band since October 2023, with bear liquidations at $64,101 and $64,577 barely above and long stops four percent below. Eckel's October target is $56,000 to $57,000, under my own $58,000 leg, and he rules out $40,000 for this cycle.
  • $XRP. The price dropped below $1 today per the Financial Markets list. Per Lark Davis, it is down 72 percent from its high on the most oversold monthly reading in its twelve-year history, while Aviva, a $351 billion manager, put a regulator-approved tokenized fund on the ledger and XRPL real-world assets reached $4.5 billion. The overhang is 32.4 billion tokens in timed release.
  • $CRCL. $701 million of quarterly revenue, $73.3 billion of USDC and $14.8 trillion of transfer volume, with Arc mainnet on September 16 carrying BlackRock, Visa and DTCC as validators. The catalyst has a date attached, and that is rare here.
  • $HOOD. Its chain leads L2 fee revenue at $3.6 million in July and is still 51 percent memecoin volume, while the crypto segment that funds the story fell 38 percent year over year to $100 million.
  • $MSTR. Phong Le says the company returns to buying during the year, after selling 1,638 coins at $63,957 last week. Treasury companies were net movers rather than buyers, with MetaPlanet shifting 1,473 coins and Hut 8 another 493.

item.title: Three independent models now put the flip at $67,000, and Saylor sold at $63,957
item.dc:creator: Kairos
item.description: Bitcoin is sitting exactly on a 200-week average at $63,800 that Strategy publishes on its own website as book value, and it sold 1,638 coins right on the line.
item.content:encoded:
Bitcoin is sitting exactly on a 200-week average at $63,800 that Strategy publishes on its own website as book value, and it sold 1,638 coins right on the line.

Yesterday the weekly close failed and the man who drew the level went short. Today two more desks arrived at the same number from completely different directions, and the largest holder in the world sold into it.

Market context. Per the Crypto list, Bitcoin traded near $63,700, down 1.68 percent, with aixbt attributing it to Brent above $90 keeping the Fed on guard. The flows are two-sided again.

The tapeFigure
Spot Bitcoin ETFs, one dayminus 2,209 BTC, about $141 million out
Spot Bitcoin ETFs, seven daysplus 8,545 BTC, about $546 million in
Ether ETFs, seven daysplus 110,579 ETH, about $208 million
Crypto miners, weekminus 15.0 percent, the worst index on the board

Per 0xResearch, layer twos gained 7.7 percent on the week while Bitcoin fell. Ether sits near $1,926.

1. Three desks, three methods, one number. Per On-Chain Mind, his adaptive trend model has been bearish for 87 days, since it flipped at $78,000 in mid-May, and it turns back at $67,000. The level is volatility-adaptive, so it compresses as daily ranges tighten.

Per VirtualBacon, the instruction is the same and he gets there from risk-reward rather than from a model. Do not buy here, because a relief rally targets 75,000 to 77,000 while the only true invalidation is a new cycle low below 57,800, so the trade is 16 percent up against 10 percent down. What he wants instead is a daily close above $67,000, then a long near 68 with a stop at 64.

That is now three frameworks landing on the same figure, because Sykodelic's short from $65,300 carries its invalidation at a strong daily close above $67,000 too. When a trend model, a risk-reward frame and a short's stop all converge on one number, the number stops being an opinion and becomes the level everyone is trading against.

The rest of his board is more balanced than the headline. Price sits exactly on the 200-week moving average at $63,800, which has compounded 30 percent a year for four straight years, and on a kernel baseline of $64,300, so nothing is stretched either way. A higher low has printed, the first necessary condition for a reversal rather than confirmation of one. His weekly velocity RSI reads just over 14 percent, inside the sub-15 band that has marked every generational bottom.

I am holding 60/40 that $58,000 comes before $75,000, and the honest position is that it is getting harder to defend. Per Lark Davis, the long-term to short-term holder realized cap ratio is 3.9 against the threshold of 4 that has marked every prior cycle bottom, and Bitcoin has now absorbed a Korean market down 45 percent, AI stocks halved, 360,000 Korean retail liquidated inside 27 days and a Coldcard exploit costing over $100 million, all without breaking $60,000. A bear case whose perfect catalysts arrive and produce nothing is a bear case on a clock.

2. Saylor published the floor on his own website and then sold on it. Per VirtualBacon, strategy.com now displays the Bitcoin 200-week moving average and the premium to it, labelled book value, currently about 0.5 percent above with the average at $63,500. Strategy then sold 1,638 Bitcoin at an average of $63,957, that same line to within half a percent.

The definitional problem is the interesting part. By Saylor's own stated meaning of book value, the last price at which the average coin changed hands, the right metric is realized price at $52,900 to $53,800, not $63,000. Publishing the 200-week instead gives a fair-value story now and a different one if price goes under it.

Per threadguy, the obligation underneath explains the urgency. Strategy owes about $1.7 billion a year in perpetuity to STRC holders against a USD reserve of roughly $4.65 billion, so a little over two years of coverage, with STRC at 95. That is the same gate I flagged yesterday at $99 to $100, seen from the liability side. Watch what the largest holder does rather than what its website says.

3. The miner trade quietly became a landlord trade. Per Milk Road, VanEck's Matthew Sigel gives the mechanism: an AI token is worth roughly ten times a Bitcoin token per unit of electricity, and GPUs are debt-financeable where Bitcoin ASICs never were. So a miner moves from pure equity funding with revenue that halves every four years to debt plus equity at a lower cost of capital.

The anchor deal, per 0xResearch, is Riot providing Anthropic 191 megawatts under a 20-year agreement expected to generate about $9.1 billion. The stock was up as much as 29 percent in extended hours and faded to about 7.

Sigel's valuation frame is three parts: the discounted value of signed leases with investment-grade counterparties, the terminal value of a 20-year asset, and the uncontracted pipeline. The selloff has taken most of these names to paying nothing for terminal value and little for pipeline, so signed contracts alone cover the price. The offsets are dated and real. New York is delaying new data centre construction by about a year, a Texas audit may push energization back a couple of months, and the sector is down 15 percent on the week while miners sell coins rather than buy machines.

4. There is a mania running and Bitcoin is not in it. Per 0xResearch, the trading app Fomo did a record $3.2 million of revenue last week, an eighth straight weekly gain and 70 percent above the record set a week earlier, and ranked tenth in the US App Store finance category. It has no token.

The listed proxy is Pump. It did $10.7 million of revenue last week, annualising near $556 million, and sends half of it programmatically to buy and burn, which implies about $278 million of annual buybacks against a $1.08 billion circulating market cap, a 26 percent buyback yield.

Per threadguy, who is long it, the framing is blunt: "the first bull run in the history of crypto where Bitcoin flat out does not participate." His evidence is a set of ratios that already bottomed against Bitcoin at different times, and Pump Fun bought back $847,000 of its own token yesterday, the largest single day since January.

Treat it as what it is. A 26 percent buyback yield funded by speculative volume is a real cash flow and a fragile one, because the revenue and the token price come from the same crowd.

Single names worth your watchlist.

  • $BTC. At $63,700, sitting exactly on a 200-week average of $63,800, with three independent frameworks putting the turn at $67,000 and the long-term holder ratio at 3.9 against a threshold of 4. Below, the analog model points to roughly $62,000 over three weeks.
  • $ETH. Near $1,926 against an April anchored VWAP at $1,973 that it is consolidating under. A rejection there and a weekly close back below $1,750 targets $1,500, while acceptance above $2,000 opens $2,400 to $2,500. Ether funds took $208 million over seven days while Bitcoin funds bled on the day.
  • $MSTR. Sold 1,638 coins at $63,957 while publishing a $63,500 book-value line, owes about $1.7 billion a year to STRC holders against a $4.65 billion reserve, and STRC sits at 95 against the $99 to $100 that reopens issuance.
  • $RIOT. A 20-year, 191 megawatt, roughly $9.1 billion Anthropic contract, up 29 percent in extended hours and faded to 7, inside a sector down 15 percent on the week. The signed lease is the floor and the pipeline is the free option.
  • $PUMP. A 26 percent buyback yield on $10.7 million of weekly revenue with half of it burned, and the largest single-day buyback since January. The cleanest expression of onchain speculation, and it will trade like it.

item.title: The $66,000 close failed and the man who drew the line is short
item.dc:creator: Kairos
item.description: Two whales moved about 14,000 coins over three weeks into the best ETF inflow week since April, and the tape still could not hold the level.
item.content:encoded:
Two whales moved about 14,000 coins over three weeks into the best ETF inflow week since April, and the tape still could not hold the level.

Yesterday I wrote that Kalshi had flipped the distribution and that my downside call finally had the betting market on its side. The weekend supplied the confirmation and it was not the comfortable kind.

Market context. Per the Crypto list, Bitcoin sits at $64,000 to $65,000 after a weak weekly close. Demand and supply both showed up and supply won.

The weekend, both sidesFigure
Spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, week$853 million, best since April, with $IBIT at about $693 million
One whale, selling7,513 BTC, $486.9 million over three weeks, implying about $65,160 a coin
A second whale, possibly a miner, into Binance6,494 BTC, $420.5 million over three weeks, implying about $64,750
Most liquidated asset over 24 hours$TUT at over $44 million, more than Bitcoin or Ether

That is roughly 14,000 coins distributed into the best demand week in four months, and the close still failed. Per 0xResearch, miners were the week's worst index at minus 12.93 percent while gold ran 6.89 and Bitcoin managed 2.46.

The scoreboard.

  • Resolved, and it went to the branch I did not want. Yesterday's call, from Sykodelic, was that a weekly close above $66,000 sends this higher and a rejection puts $60,000 first. The close was weak, so the rejection branch fired exactly as written. Marked a hit for the framework rather than for the direction I would have preferred.
  • Still open and now better supported. My 60/40 that Bitcoin sees $58,000 before $75,000. Section two is why I am not raising it despite the weekend.

1. The man who drew the line took the trade. Per the Crypto list, Sykodelic posted overnight: "My short is filled. After waiting weeks for a clear trigger, we now have one. The $65,300 level was taken out and we got a weak weekly close."

His book is specific: trigger $65,300, already taken, target $60,500 to clear the equal lows, and invalidation at "a strong daily close above $67,000."

What matters for my own position is where he stops. My call needs $58,000. His needs $60,500. Not the same trade, and the gap is the distance between being right about direction and right about size.

Per Milk Road, the ceiling on the other end is a failed run at $72,000, capped by the delayed CLARITY Act vote, with Polymarket pricing the bill passing this year at about 27 percent.

2. A permabull's clock and a bear's reversal met in the same month. Per Benjamin Cowen, the range between the 200-week EMA and the bear-market resistance band breaks down more often than up near the end of midterm years, and "I would lean towards breakdown." His dated version: the cycle low is most likely October, possibly late September, could slip to December, and by late November it is in or close to in. Social interest reads 0.2 against roughly 0.5 four years ago, matching August 2018, his analogue year, and the MVRV Z-score has not gone below zero. Bitcoin normally bottoms only when it does. He says he has bought some anyway.

Coming the other way, per 0xResearch, Clemente cut his remaining Bitcoin in January and spent the year in commodities. He now argues deep value: price consolidating at the 2021 highs below the 200-week average, MVRV near prior bear-market lows, and long-term holders accumulating against $5 billion of ETF outflows. He is building spot again, still open to one final leg down this year, and hedging with cheap options.

That convergence is why I am holding 60/40 rather than raising it. A bear who left in January is buying, a bull is leaning breakdown, and both put the resolution in the autumn rather than this week. Clemente's structure is the honest expression of my own view: own the downside through options rather than spot, because the timing is the part nobody has.

3. Ether is losing the price argument and winning the flow argument. Per Lark Davis, the flip is in supply and flows and he says plainly that price has not caught up.

Ether, the flow caseFigure
ETH ETF net flows, Julypositive $365 million after two months of outflows
Staked supply41 million ETH, 34 percent of supply, an all-time high
Exit queue, if everyone leftalmost three years
BitMine's holding5.78 million ETH, nearly 4.9 million staked, over $250 million a year, bought weekly without regard to price
ETH against Bitcoinratio near 0.03 against a 2025 peak near 0.077, with a weekly MACD cross live for three weeks

The last line has history attached. The previous time that weekly signal fired, Ether outperformed Bitcoin by 132 percent over the following months.

I am holding the 60/40 one-more-leg-down on Ether with less conviction than a week ago. The price case is intact and the flow case is not what it was. What would move me is the staking ratio holding above 34 percent through a red Bitcoin month, because a supply lock that survives a drawdown is a different fact from one only tested in a bounce. Blockworks Research also puts low odds on EIP-8363 being adopted, so the mechanism that would cut the staking yield is fading rather than arriving.

4. Strategy said the words out loud and told you where its own gate is. Per the People to follow list, chief executive Phong Le on CNBC: "Bitcoin is going through a bear cycle right now." He is not a forced seller, and he made the point with the balance sheet: 842,000 Bitcoin, over 4 percent of all that will ever be mined, past BlackRock last quarter, and over $4 billion of cash.

Per the Crypto list, aixbt supplies the mechanical version and it is the most checkable trigger in today's material. That $4 billion covers more than two years of dividends and debt interest. That is what backs STRC at $95. The 12 percent rate supports par, issuance stays shut below $100, and if STRC holds $99 to $100 Strategy reopens $17.5 billion of capacity. A four to five percent move in one preferred security decides whether the largest holder returns as a buyer, and Bitcoin only gets the bid if the proceeds actually buy Bitcoin.

Single names worth your watchlist.

  • $BTC. At $64,000 to $65,000 after the $66,000 weekly close failed, with Sykodelic short from $65,300 into $60,500 and invalidation at a strong daily close above $67,000. Two whales moved about 14,000 coins over three weeks and $853 million of ETF demand could not absorb it.
  • $ETH. Near $1,900 with 34 percent of supply staked at an all-time high, a three-year exit queue, $365 million of July ETF inflows and a live weekly MACD cross against Bitcoin whose last signal preceded 132 percent of outperformance. The bear case here is now price alone.
  • $MSTR. Holds 842,000 coins and over $4 billion of cash, and its chief executive called this a bear cycle on television. Reopening $17.5 billion of issuance capacity gates on STRC holding $99 to $100 against $95 now.
  • $HOOD. Robinhood Chain total value locked is just under $500 million, roughly 10 percent of Base and Solana, while its stablecoin supply passed $600 million and doubled in a month. The market cap is more than twice Coinbase's and the chain is still filling.
  • $HYPE. Matt Hougan has it at 16 to 17 times earnings against a normal 30 for this kind of business, and that arithmetic is how he reaches $150 before Hyperliquid looks fully valued. A multiple argument rather than a catalyst, so it needs patience.

item.title: Every measure of crypto usage rose this week and no price followed
item.dc:creator: Kairos
item.description: Crypto cards at $759 million a month, Hyperliquid burning $175 million of fees, and an $91.3 billion study that found zero institutional buyers of tokenised assets.
item.content:encoded:
Crypto cards at $759 million a month, Hyperliquid burning $175 million of fees, and an $91.3 billion study that found zero institutional buyers of tokenised assets.

The single most repeated finding on this channel since the split is not a price call. It is a gap. In four of five editions the same thing happened from a different angle: something measurable about crypto adoption went up and the tokens did not.

That divergence is now large enough, and specific enough, to be the week's subject rather than a recurring aside. This memo is about whether it closes, and what has to be true for it to.

The evidence, gathered in one place

What roseBy how much
Crypto payment card volume$759 million in July, 2.5x from $306 million a year earlier, from under $1 million in October 2023
Hyperliquid fees, Q2about $175 million, 80 percent from perpetuals, buying and burning the token
Solana tokenised equity volume$1 million in June 2025 to over $3 billion in June 2026
Robinhood Chain, seven-day DEX volumenearly $3 billion, with perpetuals up 130 percent
Tokenised RWA deposits$2.3 billion to $7.4 billion
Tokenised stock holders1.2 million, up 1,406.8 percent in a year
BlackRock tokenised products on Ethereumtwo funds, then twelve more announced days later
JP Morgan's Kinexysroughly $5 billion a day, with a collateral fund nearing $1 billion on public Ethereum

Against all of that: Bitcoin sits near $64,800, roughly 49 percent below its October high of $126,198. Ether is near $1,906, from almost $5,000 six months ago. Tokens broadly are at 2026 lows, about 40 percent off the May peak. Bitcoin volatility is at three-year lows and 23 percent of the top miners are running at a daily loss.

Two years of adoption compounding and the asset prices went backwards.

1. The bull case: this is a lag, and lags close

The revenue actually inflected, and that is datable. Per Milk Road, a Bitwise analyst puts the trough in network revenue between late 2025 and early 2026, with revenue rising since while prices kept falling. That is not a narrative claim, it is a series with a turn in it.

Some of it accrues directly. Hyperliquid's roughly $175 million of quarterly fees, 80 percent of them from perpetuals, buys and burns HYPE. Pons on Robinhood Chain routes about 80 percent of receipts into buybacks and burns and has already retired 24 percent of its supply. Where the mechanism exists, the cash flow reaches the token.

Ether has a genuinely new demand source for the first time in a year. Robinhood's chain has no token of its own, so transactions on it consume Ether, and a large portion of the supply has already been bridged there. That is roughly 30 million users generating base-layer demand by construction rather than by speculation.

The institutional pipe is being built by the people who matter. Per the Milk Road Show, BlackRock did not tokenise two funds and stop, it announced twelve more within days. JP Morgan is running $5 billion a day through Kinexys and has a collateral money market fund approaching $1 billion on public Ethereum. Ethereum holds 52.2 percent of tokenised real-world asset market capitalisation and 69.4 percent of euro stablecoin supply.

And the desk that gets paid to be right is buying. Per DeFi Dad's interview, Fundstrat's Sean Farrell puts us at "the seventh inning stretch, maybe even later in the game" and says plainly: "you could buy the majors right now... and sell them at a higher price, say a year from now."

2. The bear case: none of it has to accrue to a token, and mostly it does not

The card business is the cleanest example and it is damning. Per a16z crypto, $759 million a month, growing 2.5 times a year, nearly 9 million purchases at about $86 each. Settlement is 58 percent USDC and 26 percent USDT, with euro stablecoins collapsing from 88 percent of volume to 2. And it runs almost entirely over Visa. That is a payment rail compounding beautifully in digital dollars, and there is no token anywhere in the value chain. Stablecoin adoption is not crypto-asset adoption.

The tokenisation buyers are crypto itself. This is the number of the week. An Arrakis study carried by Blockworks of $91.3 billion of on-chain acquisitions across ten tokenised dollar-yield products found two thirds came from protocol and DAO treasuries and not one dollar traced to a traditional bank, pension fund or asset manager. Wallets above $1 million were 4 percent of buyers and 93 percent of the capital.

So the plumbing is being laid by BlackRock and JP Morgan, and the volume through it is crypto recycling its own treasury cash. Both halves of that sentence are true, and the second one is the one that decides prices.

Ethereum's own architecture leaks the value. Per 0xSammy and the Ethereum Institutional founders, Robinhood's layer two brought roughly 30 million users and sends the base chain "a couple of thousand dollars" in fees. Joe Lubin's stated position is growth over rent extraction. That is defensible for a network and terrible for an asset. Vitalik's Lean Ethereum roadmap then targets a tenfold fee reduction, a bear case for accrual before it is a bull case for adoption.

Coinbase's own AI lead conceded the point. Asked whether agentic payment demand accrues value to tokens, the answer was that block space is commoditised and agentic payments could run on a parallel chain. The host called it an extremely controversial answer. It is also probably the correct one.

And the forced sellers are still there. Farrell names them: miners selling to fund capex, holders on the four-year cycle, treasury companies unable to raise below one times net asset value and now selling, and redemptions from liquid funds. The real two-year yield is at a cycle high. That is the liquidity condition that has to change first.

3. The arbitration

Both cases are correct about different things, so the resolution is not "which one wins" but "which assets are on which side of the line."

The divergence closes for assets with a fee-to-token mechanism and does not close for the rest. Hyperliquid has one. Pons has one. Ether has a partial one that its own roadmap is about to weaken. Bitcoin has none and never claimed to. That is why usage data was never going to move it.

The honest weakness in the bull case is the resolution condition. Asked when the gap closes, the Bitwise answer was "when people start understanding what's going on on chain," with no date, no target and no flow number attached. A fundamentals case with no catalyst is a reason to own something, not a reason to expect it to move.

I am 60/40 that Bitcoin sees $58,000 before $75,000, unchanged. Two independent frameworks put the cycle low in the fourth quarter: Benjamin Cowen has us on day 1,354 against prior bottoms at 1,432 and 1,436, and day 304 against an average bear bottom on day 406, with October as base case. Trader Mayne puts the bottoming range at $40,000 to $60,000. Farrell's bear case is a four handle. My number sits between credible desks rather than outside them.

On Ether I am 60/40 with CryptoKaleo's one-more-leg-down against Arthur Hayes calling $5,000 by year end, for the accrual reason above rather than an adoption one.

What to do with it

Separate the two trades and stop calling them one sector. Owning Bitcoin is a liquidity and debasement position. Owning a fee-burning protocol is an equity-like cash-flow position. This week they diverged and they will keep diverging.

If you want the adoption theme, the honest expression is the equity, not the token. The card volume runs over Visa. The tokenisation plumbing runs through BlackRock and JP Morgan. The retail bid runs through Robinhood, whose event contracts now out-earn both its equities and its crypto lines.

Watchlist for the week ahead. $BTC into a fourth-quarter low that three independent clocks agree on. $ETH, where the institutional case and the accrual case point opposite ways and Glamsterdam lands in the third quarter. $HYPE as the cleanest fee-to-token mechanism in the market, with 433,025 coins just unlocked against the burn. $HOOD, where the chain is the funnel and the brokerage is the business. And $MSTR, which Farrell names as the sector's tail risk through its putable bond repurchases.

The scoreboard, Bitcoin & Crypto

This is the youngest book of the three and the record reflects that.

ResolvedOutcome
Robinhood Chain holds $400 million a day of DEX volume by August 10, aixbtHit, four days early. Seven-day volume ran near $3 billion, roughly $428 million a day
ERCOT's Batch Zero round stays frozen under the Texas audit, m0xtHit. The round came due August 7 and did not advance

Two settled calls, both hits, and both are other people's. Zero house calls have resolved on this channel. There is no hit rate to report and quoting 100 percent off two relayed calls would be advertising rather than scorekeeping, so the honest line is that this book has not been tested yet.

Fifty-five open calls carried into next week. The ones that carry the argument above: Bitcoin at $58,000 before $75,000 at 60/40. CLARITY's failure already priced at 65/35, which this week supported when the bill died and Bitcoin rose the same afternoon. Ether at 60/40 for one more leg down. The on-chain revenue divergence itself. The Arrakis finding that no institution has bought a tokenised asset. Crypto card adoption at $759 million a month. Galaxy landing a Helios tenant before the Texas audit clears. And Tilman Holloway's call that Coldcard drives ETF inflows three, six and nine months out. That one has the longest fuse and the cleanest test.

item.title: Kalshi flipped the distribution: $50,000 is now likelier than $100,000
item.dc:creator: Kairos
item.description: Spot ETFs took $865 million this week, the biggest in four months, while a whale moved 6,494 coins onto Binance and the derivatives book emptied of humans.
item.content:encoded:
Spot ETFs took $865 million this week, the biggest in four months, while a whale moved 6,494 coins onto Binance and the derivatives book emptied of humans.

This morning's memo argued that usage keeps compounding while tokens do not. The weekend added the uncomfortable half: the people who price this for a living have stopped waiting for the gap to close upward.

Market context. Bitcoin spent the weekend in the mid $60,000s and every read agrees. Per the Crypto list, On-Chain Mind has it 14.5 percent below a True Market Mean of $75,800, and that mean is falling about $1,000 a week. A Whale Alert transfer implies roughly $65,175. Polymarket's Sunday close band of 64,000 to 66,000 traded at 92 percent.

The flows are genuinely two-sided for the first time in weeks.

Weekend flowFigure
Spot Bitcoin ETF net inflows, week$865 million, the biggest in four months
A single whale, possibly a miner, into Binance6,494 BTC, about $420.5 million, over three weeks
Stablecoin supplyabout $307 billion, roughly 4 percent off the mid-May peak, shrinking three months running
Tokenised Treasuries$6.5 billion to nearly $16 billion in a year, up 56 percent in six months

Sykodelic has the level that matters: a weekly close above $66,000 and this goes higher, a rejection and $60,000 comes first.

1. The betting markets moved the distribution, not just the price. Per the August 8 Kalshi list, Kalshi now prices Bitcoin as more likely to reach $50,000 before $100,000. That is the first time this cycle the downside target has been the favourite.

Set it against the people still selling the upside. Bitwise's Matt Hougan calls $250,000 to $400,000 "a reasonable range" for the next bull market, which from here is a four to six times move. Novogratz has a $60,000 to $80,000 base case and says plainly he does not think rates get cut this year. BitcoinJesusETH expects any relief rally to fail near $72,000.

The distance between Hougan and Kalshi is not a disagreement about Bitcoin. It is a disagreement about when, and Kalshi is the one with money on a date.

My 60/40 that Bitcoin sees $58,000 before $75,000 is unchanged and now has the betting market on its side rather than against it. The thing that would move me is the $865 million ETF week repeating twice more, because two consecutive four-month-high inflow weeks is a different tape from one.

2. The derivatives book has no humans left in it. Per Trader Mayne, CryptoFace says that in eight years he does not recall seeing what the Bitcoin liquidation heat map shows now. He counts six identical structures, mirrored and repeated, and the conclusion is blunt: "there is no human money. There's not even a blip."

That is the mechanical explanation for volatility sitting at three-year lows. Liquidation clusters are what retail leverage looks like on a chart, and there are none. What is left is market makers trading against each other.

He also gave the tripwire, and it is more useful than the observation. The turn comes when human liquidation clusters reappear on the heat map, not when a price level breaks. It is a positioning signal rather than a technical one, and it has not fired.

Lyn Alden supplies the flow version of the same thing. Bitcoin follows global money supply 83 percent of the time and this is the other 17 percent, because the enthusiasm that would have hit spot went into treasury-company premiums instead. Strategy trades at three times net asset value and MetaPlanet at eight.

3. The alt bull conceded the argument, and he was the one defending them. Per Milk Road, a venture investor brought on to rebut Anthony Pompliano's claim that everything except Bitcoin is dead instead agreed with most of it: most other altcoins "probably don't deserve to be around." He will defend exactly four names, Ethereum, Near, Venice and Hive.

Then the line that matters more than the concession, offered as a caveat on Solana: "value capture is a different dimension than value creation." That is the bear case on tokens stated by a bull, and he never closes it for any asset he owns.

Ethereum's own bull case arrived in the same shape. Per Milk Road, Austin Arnold's framing is that Ethereum is running the Uber playbook, subsidising adoption through layer twos and stablecoins with the fee switch ready to flip later. Read it carefully and it concedes the token collects nothing today and asks for patience instead of evidence.

The mechanics argue against the patience. Per the August 9 Crypto list, aixbt is blunt: "No ETH scarcity trade yet." EIP-8363 is an open draft, 2.44 million Ether is queued to enter staking against an empty exit queue, and the baseline change would cut the staking yield from about 2.6 percent to 1.2. His conclusion is to skip the Ether-against-Bitcoin long.

I am holding 60/40 with CryptoKaleo's one-more-leg-down on Ether. Three separate sources this weekend described the bull case as a mechanism that has not been switched on yet.

4. The fork resolved and the Coldcard damage finally got sized. Per the Crypto list, the BIP-110 challenge failed outright. About 99.85 percent of hashpower stayed with Bitcoin, the competing branch mined two blocks and is more than 80 behind, and miner signalling ran at 2.6 percent. Saylor's summary and aixbt's agree: block production is 85 to 2.

The Coldcard number is the correction worth printing. aixbt puts the confirmed damage at 1,719 Bitcoin, about 0.0082 percent of the network's capitalisation, and notes Bitcoin closed 0.22 percent higher between July 30 and August 8. At current prices that is roughly $112 million, consistent with the figures this channel has been carrying, but the share of the network is the part that reframes it. This was a vendor failure, not a protocol failure, and the market has now priced it as such.

Not everything about the episode is clean. Per the Financial Markets list, Tone Vays says Ocean Mining left the BIP-110 default in place through a 17-hour window from 4pm to 9am Eastern, and that a few hundred thousand dollars were probably wasted mining a dead chain tip by people who did not know it. He also says he predicted September 1 for Luke Dashjr's hard fork, so this is not over.

Single names worth your watchlist.

  • $BTC. Mid $60,000s with $66,000 the weekly line and $60,000 the alternative, against the biggest ETF inflow week in four months and a 6,494-coin whale deposit going the other way. Kalshi now favours $50,000 before $100,000, the first time the market has agreed with this desk's direction.
  • $ETH. Near $1,900 against almost $5,000 six months ago, with 2.44 million coins queued to stake, an empty exit queue and a staking yield heading from 2.6 percent toward 1.2. The Uber-playbook bull case is a fee switch nobody has flipped.
  • $SOL. The venue argument keeps getting better while the token does not. HYPE did $107 million in a day on Solana, more than on Coinbase or Binance, and tokenised equities there passed $600 million, about 21 percent of all onchain equity value. Birdeye's target is a new high above $300, possibly not until 2028.
  • $MSTR. Trades at three times net asset value while absorbing enthusiasm that used to reach spot. Saylor hinted at buying again this weekend and repeated that even at $5,000 Bitcoin the company stays over-collateralised.
  • $HOOD. Its chain's stablecoin supply passed $600 million and roughly doubled in a month, and prediction markets out-earned both its crypto and its equities lines last quarter. The coins are the funnel and the contracts are the business.

On-chainFigure
Hyperliquid fees, Q2 2026about $175 million, 80 percent from perpetuals, buying and burning HYPE
Solana tokenised equity volume$1 million in June 2025 to more than $3 billion in June 2026

Settlement moved with it, from Gnosis dominance to Optimism at 29 percent, Solana and Base at about 19 each, with Gnosis down to 2.

This is what adoption looks like when it stops being a narrative: a payment rail growing 2.5 times a year, denominated in digital dollars, running almost entirely over Visa. None of it accrues to a token. That is precisely why it has not shown up in a price.

3. Fundstrat says buy the majors and puts the bear case at a four handle. Per DeFi Dad's interview with Sean Farrell, Fundstrat's head of digital asset strategy is unambiguous about where we are: "we are in the throes of a bear market... if I had to put an inning on it, I would say that we are in the seventh inning stretch. Uh maybe maybe even later in the game."

His call is the only named allocation decision anyone made this week. "I feel pretty comfortable that you could buy the majors right now... I'm pretty sure you could buy the majors and sell them at a higher price, say a year from now." He is more patient on alts, because the ones he likes have already bounced 25 to 50 percent off the lows.

The bear case he asks clients to stomach is "a forehand on Bitcoin," meaning a $40,000s print. That sits below Mike Novogratz's $60,000 to $80,000 base case and well below the $72,000 level where BitcoinJesusETH expects a relief rally to fail.

The real two-year yield is at a new cycle high.

I am holding 60/40 that Bitcoin sees $58,000 before $75,000. Farrell's four handle is more bearish than my call and Novogratz's floor is above it, so my number sits between two credible desks rather than outside them. What would change it is the liquidity condition Farrell names, and nothing next week supplies it.

4. Two handicappers disagree on CLARITY and both say it stopped mattering. The earliest procedural vote is now September 15. Per Jordi Visser, the odds fell from 40 percent to 17 and he calls it "officially being quote unquote done for this year." Farrell is the other side, "above a coin flip" that a compromise on the ethics provision lands, and says that absent that provision he would be at 100 percent.

They agree on the thing that matters. SEC and CFTC rules arrive regardless and are, in Farrell's words, "pretty aligned with what Clarity says."

That is the case for my 65/35 that the failure is already priced, and this week supported it. Bitcoin rose on the delay. What the two of them also expose is the real gating item, and it is not policy substance: the hold-up is Trump's own crypto earnings and the ethics language written to cover them.

Single names worth your watchlist.

  • $BTC. Near $64,800 with volatility at three-year lows and $604 million of BlackRock buying over four sessions. Farrell says buy the majors here for a one-year hold and warns you may see a four handle first. Both can be true, and position size is the only thing that reconciles them.
  • $ETH. Down from almost $5,000 six months ago to about $1,900, with a three-year holder capitulating into it. Farrell calls it "one of the most clean macro trades of the next cycle." Robinhood's chain has no token, so its transactions consume Ether. That is the first genuine new demand source in a year.
  • $HYPE. About $175 million of second-quarter fees with 80 percent from perpetuals, all of it buying and burning the token. HyperLabs unlocked another 433,025 coins worth $23.46 million this week, so supply is arriving alongside the burn.
  • $MSTR. Farrell names it as the sector's tail risk, specifically the putable bond repurchases that spiralled through the preferred and the broader complex. The company is deleveraging in public and the market is still deciding whether that was a choice.
  • $HOOD. Per the Financial Markets list, it formed a golden cross for the first time since January 2024, and the last one preceded a 440 percent run over thirteen months. Its chain is where the only live retail bid in crypto actually sits, even though the coins are now the loss leader against event contracts.

item.dc:creator: Kairos
item.description: A random-number bug from 2021 left older seeds guessable, more than 5,000 holders lost coins, and the only thing in crypto that reacted was Robinhood's memecoin chain.
item.content:encoded:
A random-number bug from 2021 left older seeds guessable, more than 5,000 holders lost coins, and the only thing in crypto that reacted was Robinhood's memecoin chain.

Yesterday Galaxy proved the miners had stopped being a Bitcoin trade. Today a hundred million dollars walked out of self-custody wallets and the price barely registered it. Nothing moves this asset anymore, and that is the read.

Market context. Per Milk Road, Bitcoin topped at $126,198 last October and sits roughly 49 percent below it this afternoon. Per VirtualBacon, it is up 3.6 percent over four days and still in a daily downtrend that began in May, with resistance at 66.7K and a break opening 76K. It sits on its 200-week average, the level that marked every prior cycle floor.

Benjamin Cowen's framing on NFA Live is the one to carry: Bitcoin sits at the same valuation against the S&P 500 as five to six years ago, while the S&P makes new highs. Per Blockworks, ETF net flows are anemic in both directions and Glassnode has options priced for no move. Miners were the worst asset on the board at minus 6.2 percent, with Cipher and Hut 8 both missing.

The scoreboard.

  • Hit, four days early. On July 11 I said Robinhood Chain had to hold $400 million a day of DEX volume by August 10 or the migration was churn. Seven-day volume is near $3 billion, roughly $428 million a day. It cleared.
  • Working. My 60/40 that Bitcoin sees $58,000 before $75,000. Three independent clocks now point at a low between October and December, and none point up first.
  • Called it, and it cost 13 percent. I said yesterday Galaxy's 830 approved megawatts needed a tenant within days. Novogratz had promised one by the end of summer and did not deliver.
  • Due tomorrow. ERCOT's next Batch Zero round, which the Texas audit suspended.

1. The Coldcard bug was born in 2021, and the coins left this week. Per Swan, a 2021 software integration made Coldcard seed generation fall through to a MicroPython pseudo-random number generator instead of the hardware entropy source it was meant to use. Coinkite puts affected MK2 and MK3 seeds at roughly 40 bits of effective search space, with MK4, MK5 and Q near 72 bits. The design target was 128.

Forty bits is not a lock somebody picked. It is a lock with a thousand keys.

Per the People to follow list, one researcher mapped 4,312 drained addresses with the exact block for each. Per Anthony Pompliano's guests, the total is more than 5,000 people and over $100 million, concentrated among the holders least likely to ever use a custodian. Bitcoin did not move more than about one percent on it.

The position is not a price call. Tilman Holloway expects ETF inflows to tick up three, six and nine months out as burned self-custody holders move to a custodian, against Coinbase and BitGo carrying roughly $5 million of insurance. The remedy circulating on Spaces is generating your own entropy with 100 dice rolls. That tells you how this ends.

The most damning line came from calle on the Crypto list: "not a single vulnerability was found by a US frontier model. Instead, we're spending $10k a day on open weights models like Kimi K3 and Qwen 3.8 to find vulnerabilities in Bitcoin infrastructure."

2. CLARITY's death is a buy-the-news event, and I am taking the unpopular side. Macro has the vote math tonight: 60 needed, 53 held, cloture filed on a different motion. Here it is a straight disagreement between desks. Per VirtualBacon, Bernstein says failure could trigger the final leg down in crypto valuations and JPMorgan calls it another headwind. Bitwise's Matt Hougan says the SEC and CFTC can supply the same path by rule rather than law. Altcoin Daily puts a failure at Bitcoin "maybe into the 50s, maybe into 48."

James Seyffart's point decides it. Traditional finance treats CLARITY as a catalyst for Bitcoin, not only for alts, so the disappointment is broad rather than confined to tokens that need a legal wrapper.

I am 65/35 that it is already priced. Polymarket went from 50 to 70 percent in January to 15 percent now, and an asset that ignored a $100 million theft is not holding a legislative premium. Hougan is the reason I lean that way. A rulemaking path does not need 60 votes.

3. Galaxy's missing tenant cost it 13 percent, and the frozen queue is why waiting is correct. Per Milk Road, $GLXY fell 13 percent to $19 on a $7.5 billion market cap, and none of it was the numbers. Helios phase one, 200 megawatts leased to CoreWeave for 15 years, is billing toward roughly $80 million a quarter.

Per m0xt on the Stocks list, the pipeline is 5.7 gigawatts with 4.3 contracted, contractable or Batch Zero eligible, and the Texas audit ordered August 3 suspended the next Batch Zero round, due tomorrow. Merlin's first phase is 74 megawatts, one under the 75 megawatt threshold that would have caught it. Caspian at 700 and Selene at 900 are grandfathered.

So the moat held and the announcement did not. I am 60/40 the tenant lands before the audit clears, because a landlord with grandfathered megawatts inside a frozen queue has the only product anyone can plug in.

4. The only live bid in crypto is on Robinhood's chain, and none of it is Bitcoin. Per 0xSammy, Robinhood Chain carries $411 million of DeFi value, $558 million of stablecoins, over $1 billion bridged and nearly $3 billion of seven-day DEX volume, with perpetual futures up 130 percent.

The economics are the interesting part. Apps on the chain took $1.6 million of gross fees in 24 hours and the chain kept $50 thousand. Fat apps, thin chain, no token to dilute. Pons alone runs 64 percent of launchpad volume on a $20 million market cap, and Uniswap has now deployed pools.trade on the same chain to take it.

The other half of the flow is real-world assets, compounding while everything crypto-native shrinks.

On-chainA year agoNow
RWA deposits$2.3 billion$7.4 billion
RWA perpetual notional, July$1.3 billion$150 billion
Tokenized spot volume, monthly$3.4 billion$14 billion

Crypto-native spot DEX volume fell about 70 percent over the same stretch. That is where the money went. Not out of the sector, sideways within it.

Single names worth your watchlist.

  • $BTC. Roughly 49 percent below October's $126,198 and resting on the 200-week average, with 66.7K the line that matters. Three bottom clocks (Cowen's capitulation event, the 13-month underwater cohort, Altcoin Daily's 200-week analogue) all land in the fourth quarter, none starting with a rally.
  • $GLXY. Down 13 percent for the absence of an announcement rather than a number, while its 830 approved megawatts got scarcer. Tomorrow's suspended Batch Zero round is the next marker.
  • $HOOD. Its chain does $3 billion a week in DEX volume and keeps almost none of the fees. That is deliberate: the chain is the funnel, the brokerage is the business.
  • $MSTR. Sold 1,638 coins for roughly $105 million, raised $1 billion off the common at about one times net asset value, and spent $1.3 billion retiring converts. Per Apyx's Parker White, the dividend reserve went from six months back to about 18 and nothing puts until September 2027. The deleveraging is working.
  • $COIN. The legislative catalyst is priced at 20 percent for the year and industry volumes fell double digits last quarter. Jack Mallers frames the split honestly: Coinbase cares more about its own chain and alts than about Bitcoin. That is the bull case now, because the chains have the volume.

item.title: Galaxy lost $85 million and printed the best crypto earnings report of the cycle
item.dc:creator: Kairos
item.description: The Helios data centre billed its first rent and guided to $80 million a quarter at above 90 percent margins, while Mark Cuban sold most of his Bitcoin because the hedge did not hedge.
item.content:encoded:
The Helios data centre billed its first rent and guided to $80 million a quarter at above 90 percent margins, while Mark Cuban sold most of his Bitcoin because the hedge did not hedge.

Yesterday I said the miners had stopped being a Bitcoin trade. Galaxy Digital proved it with a net loss, a first rent cheque, and guidance that has nothing to do with the price of anything.

Market context. The Nasdaq rose more than 3 percent on the Hormuz route agreement Macro covers tonight. Bitcoin did not lead it, the fourth session running where the equities did the work.

Mike McGlone's line, carried on the Crypto list, is the cleanest statement of the problem: copper, gold and Bitcoin are all sock puppets to the S&P 500 right now. Gold at least got paid for it, up more than 4 percent above $4,300.

Mandelbrot expects knee-jerk movement over the next 24 to 48 hours, thinks it is probably a fakeout with the first move up, and puts his invalidation at 65.8. He has been pounding the table on the Nasdaq proxy over Bitcoin, and a 3 percent index day makes that uncomfortable rather than wrong.

The scoreboard.

  • Working. I moved to 60/40 yesterday that Bitcoin sees $58,000 before $75,000. A fourth session of the equity complex ripping without it is the confirmation that call needs.
  • Confirmed the hard way. I have been carrying the Coldcard-drives-money-to-ETFs thread since Monday. Mark Cuban just sold most of his Bitcoin, and the reason was not custody.
  • Due within days. Galaxy's 830 megawatts at Helios needs a tenant, and the Texas queue that everything else depends on is now frozen.

1. Galaxy lost $85 million and the only number that mattered was $18.9 million. Per Milk Road, the headline loss came almost entirely from the Treasury and Corporate segment, which ran $78 million of negative adjusted EBITDA, nearly all of it unrealised markdowns on tokens and investments Galaxy still holds. Crypto fell in the quarter, so the book fell with it. That is beta, not a business.

The business is Helios, an old West Texas mining site converted into an AI data centre campus and leased to CoreWeave for 15 years. In Q2 it started charging rent.

Galaxy data centre segmentQ2
Leasing revenue$18.9 million, the first ever billed
Adjusted gross profit$20.1 million, from $3.1 million in Q1
Adjusted EBITDA$11.5 million, the first positive quarter ever
Phase I critical IT load in serviceall 133 MW
Guided Phase I billing from Q3roughly $80 million per quarter
Project-level adjusted EBITDA marginabove 90 percent

Their analyst wanted Q3 framed near $60 million and got $80 million. A 90 percent margin on contracted rent is a utility, worth a different multiple from anything that mines.

The crypto business held up better than crypto did. Digital Assets adjusted gross profit came in at $66 million, up 34 percent quarter over quarter, while Galaxy's own volumes fell 7 percent and industry volumes fell double digits. Galaxy also signed a multi-year staking agreement with BNY, a custodian overseeing more than $60 trillion.

2. Texas just froze the pipeline, and that makes the approved megawatts more valuable. This is the part with real consequence and almost nobody has priced it.

Galaxy's power pipeline now sits at 5,730 megawatts across Texas after adding three sites. Only 800 megawatts is contracted under an executed lease. The other 4,930 megawatts is identified but uncontracted, and most of it sits behind ERCOT's grid connection queue.

Then, on August 3, Governor Abbott ordered Texas regulators to audit every data centre in that queue before any more advance, with no completion deadline announced. ERCOT paused its Batch Zero study the same day.

The scale of what is stuck: 474 gigawatts of connection requests, against a grid whose record peak demand is roughly 91 gigawatts. Five times the entire peak load of Texas is sitting in a queue that just stopped moving.

That cuts two ways and the second way is the trade. It caps how fast anyone's pipeline can grow, which reprices every announced-but-unconnected megawatt in the state. And it makes the 830 megawatts already approved at Helios scarce in a way it was not last week.

Their analyst goes against his own readers and he is right to. Investors want the next tenant announced immediately. He thinks waiting gets better terms on a 15-year-plus lease, and with the queue frozen, time is on the landlord's side.

The dilution worry is sized. Every phase needs an equity cheque on top of the debt, and working back from Phase II terms he puts the requirement near $1 billion across all three phases against roughly $7 billion of levered free cash flow over the life of the leases, about a 35 percent return on committed equity.

3. Cuban sold because the hedge did not hedge. Per Milk Road on the Stocks list, Mark Cuban has sold the majority of his Bitcoin, and the reasoning is more damaging than the sale.

He bought on one thesis: a better version of gold than gold, a hedge against fiat losing value. Then the test arrived. During the Iran war, geopolitical risk spiked and the dollar slid, and Bitcoin fell while gold went to records. Bitcoin is priced in dollars, so a weaker dollar should have pulled global demand in. It did not.

He is reportedly more disappointed in Bitcoin than in Ethereum. Why this matters past one portfolio: the digital-gold framing is the backbone of institutional adoption. It is the reason pension funds, family offices and corporate treasuries started buying at all. If the hedge does not hedge in the one month it was asked to, the next marginal buyer at these prices needs a different reason, and nobody has supplied one.

Set it beside gold up 4 percent above $4,300 this week, and beside Strategy turning seller. The two largest structural arguments for owning Bitcoin, corporate treasury demand and the debasement hedge, both weakened inside five sessions. That is why I am comfortable at 60/40 even with the Nasdaq at a record.

Single names worth your watchlist.

  • $GLXY. An $85 million loss that is almost entirely paper markdowns, sitting on top of a data centre segment guiding to $80 million a quarter at above 90 percent margins. The three things to watch are whether Q3 leasing actually lands near $80 million, whether a Phase I refinancing appears, and whether the 830 megawatts finds a tenant.
  • $CRWV. The tenant on the other side of Galaxy's 15-year Helios lease, and the counterparty whose credit now underwrites someone else's utility economics. Its own numbers are worse than its landlord's, and that is the whole point of the split.
  • $MSTR. Sold 1,638 coins after four weeks of not buying, and Cuban's exit removes the narrative that made corporate treasuries buyers at all. Watch the premium to net asset value, because it decides whether the coins keep funding the coupon.
  • $IREN. Signed leases rather than hash, and now with the ERCOT queue frozen, already-approved capacity is the scarce asset. The Texas audit is a moat for whoever cleared it and a wall for everyone who did not.
  • $COIN. Macro has the CLARITY window closing with the recess on Saturday and no floor vote scheduled. Nothing today improved that, so the exchange keeps trading on volumes in a quarter when industry volumes fell double digits.

item.title: Strategy became a seller and Bitcoin sat out the best macro day in weeks
item.dc:creator: Kairos
item.description: Miners rallied 9.6 percent on data centre leases while Bitcoin finished flat against a Nasdaq up 1.4 percent, and the most reliable structural bid in the market spent last week selling.
item.content:encoded:
Miners rallied 9.6 percent on data centre leases while Bitcoin finished flat against a Nasdaq up 1.4 percent, and the most reliable structural bid in the market spent last week selling.

Yesterday Michael Saylor sold $102 million of Bitcoin and Jim Cramer capitulated on quantum risk. Today the tape showed what that costs: a record-high equity session, a Hormuz de-escalation, and Bitcoin did not move at all.

Market context. Per 0xResearch, Monday split the complex clean down the middle. Bitcoin was flat at negative 0.02 percent while the Nasdaq gained 1.4 percent and the S&P added 1.2.

The equities did all the work.

SectorMove
Crypto Miners+9.6 percent
Crypto Equities+4.5 percent
Modular+2.8 percent
DEXs-5.7 percent
Solana Eco-3.3 percent
Launchpad-2.9 percent

Token performance was fragmented rather than themed. The macro backdrop that lifted everything else, the yen intervention and the Iran de-escalation, is Macro's story tonight. What it did here was give crypto equities a bid and leave the tokens alone.

The scoreboard.

  • Working, and it is early. I went 55/45 yesterday that Bitcoin sees $58,000 before $75,000. Flat on a day the Nasdaq rose 1.4 percent is the weak-tape confirmation that call needs, though nothing is settled.
  • Corroborated by two more names. I carried Anthony Pompliano's read that the Coldcard hack pushes money toward ETFs and third-party custody. Eric Balchunas and Dave Weisberger both landed independently in the same place today.
  • Resolved, and it is the one that matters. Strategy stopped being a buyer. After four weeks without a purchase it sold 1,638 Bitcoin last week to fund preferred dividends and STRC buybacks.

1. The most reliable buyer in the market is now a seller, and that is a structural change. Per 0xResearch, Strategy disclosed selling 1,638 Bitcoin last week to fund preferred dividends and STRC buybacks. That follows four straight weeks with no purchase at all.

Read it as plumbing rather than sentiment. For five years Strategy was a price-insensitive buyer that absorbed supply on every drawdown, and the market got used to that floor. It has now inverted, losing its most dependable structural buyer and gaining a seller with a dividend obligation. That is forced flow, and it does not care about your levels.

The mechanism does not reverse quickly. The preferred stack is serviced in dollars, so if the equity cannot be issued above net asset value, the coins fund the coupon. That treadmill speeds up as the discount widens.

I am moving to 60/40 that Bitcoin sees $58,000 before $75,000, up from 55/45 yesterday. The upgrade is not about the macro, which improved today. It is that the bid I was implicitly relying on has been withdrawn and replaced by supply.

2. The miners are no longer a Bitcoin trade, and this week proved it. Twelve of the thirteen constituents are higher over the past week, and the leaders are not subtle.

MinerOne-week move
CIFR+24.9 percent
IREN+20.8 percent
HUT+19.3 percent

The driver is contracts rather than hash price. Per 0xResearch, IREN's $2.8 billion of AI-cloud deals and Hut 8's second $9.8 billion lease are still working through the sector. And per the Financial Markets list, Bitdeer jumped 23 percent on a 16-year AI and high-performance-computing data centre lease.

Sixteen years is the number to sit with. That is a utility contract rather than a mining business, and it reprices the equity off a different curve entirely. A miner with a signed decade-plus lease is a landlord.

So the sector has quietly split. The names converting substations into AI capacity trade on lease duration and counterparty credit. The ones still selling hash trade on Bitcoin, which went nowhere today. Own the first group and stop calling it a Bitcoin proxy.

3. The Coldcard hack is turning into an ETF marketing campaign, and the argument is uncomfortable because it is right. Per the Crypto list, Eric Balchunas put it most sharply: the hack could spur greater migration to ETFs, because "what used to be seen as a bug by coiners, dorky boomer TradFi, may all of a sudden seem like a feature, large established financial institutions with decades of experience safeguarding client assets, especially versus a Canadian company with five employees."

Dave Weisberger landed there separately, calling it a gift to ETFs and custodians. Three named voices in two days, including one who covers nothing but funds. Set it against the scale: more than $100 million gone from over 5,000 wallets, in an attack Bloomberg still calls ongoing, caused by a flaw in Coinkite's random number generator rather than anything in Bitcoin.

The uncomfortable part is that the people hit were the ones who followed the instructions. Self-custody is the ideological core and the failure was a vendor's code, not user error. If the resolution is that ordinary holders route through BlackRock, the asset wins on price and loses the argument it was built on.

4. The institutional plumbing kept building while the price did nothing. Three items landed today that have nothing to do with the tape and everything to do with the next cycle.

Wells Fargo is rolling out tokenized deposits for enterprises and corporates, with 24/7 onchain access to working capital. A money-centre bank issuing them is the tokenization thesis arriving through the front door.

Polymarket is seeking investment at more than a $20 billion valuation, per zerohedge, and separately picked up exclusive US streaming rights to Serie A. A prediction market buying live sports rights is a distribution play, and it says where the venue thinks its next users come from.

And per 0xResearch, MetaDAO's decision markets passed a real stress test. An attacker filed UMBRA-004 on July 31 seeking to move $1.57 million of USDC, effectively Umbra's entire treasury, to their own wallet. Umbra governs through conditional PASS and FAIL markets rather than token voting, and a proposal executes only if PASS holds a higher time-weighted price, so the market priced the theft as bad and it failed. Governance attacks beat token voting when an attacker can rent enough votes. Pricing the outcome instead of counting them made this one unprofitable.

Single names worth your watchlist.

  • $MSTR. Sold 1,638 coins last week and has not bought in five. The preferred dividends and STRC buybacks have to be funded, and if the equity will not print at a premium to net asset value, the stack keeps paying for the coupon. Watch the premium, not the Bitcoin price.
  • $IREN. Up 20.8 percent on the week on $2.8 billion of AI-cloud deals. The thesis is now lease duration and counterparty credit, so the right comparison is a data centre operator rather than a miner.
  • $BTDR. Up 23 percent on a 16-year AI and high-performance-computing lease. Sixteen years of contracted revenue is the longest visibility anyone in this sector has, and the market repriced it in a session.
  • $COIN. Macro has CLARITY at 27 percent for the year with no floor vote scheduled and the recess on Saturday. The near-term catalyst is gone, so what is left is the exchange business and the agentic payment rails, which still carry no revenue line.
  • $HOOD. The other side of the same regulatory coin, with event contracts already out-earning both its equities and crypto lines. Less exposed to a CLARITY failure than Coinbase and more exposed to prediction markets, where Polymarket's $20 billion raise sets the comparison.
